title: Machine learning stratifies cognitive impairment risk in older adults with sarcopenia
summary: In 3,310 older adults with possible sarcopenia from ten hospitals, a model using traditional Chinese medicine constitution and seven Lasso-selected features reached AUC 0.853 internally and 0.799 in an independent 314-person sample. The outcome is screening-defined probable MCI by a MoCA criterion, not a clinical diagnosis, and the study is cross-sectional.
ai_technology: Lasso feature selection with MLP, gradient boosting and other classifiers, described with SHAP
organization: Chengdu University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

evidence.tested: Internal validation and an independent single-institution external sample (n=314).
evidence.unknown: Longitudinal and clinical-diagnosis performance are not tested; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Trained and compared classifiers to stratify probable MCI.
